_about: Pipeline Doctor failure library. Each entry: id, category, weight (3 = specific root cause, 2 = likely cause, 1 = symptom), confidence, pattern (Python regex, case-insensitive unless it starts with (?-i)), title (may use {named groups}), why, fix (ordered steps), owner (who can fix: developer | pipeline-admin | platform-team). Add new entries freely; keep patterns specific.

signatures.pattern: npm (ERR!|error) code ERESOLVE
signatures.title: npm peer-dependency conflict (ERESOLVE)
signatures.why: Two packages require incompatible versions of a shared peer dependency. Usually introduced by a version bump in package.json.
fix: Read the 'Could not resolve dependency' / 'peer X from Y' lines to find the two conflicting packages.
Align versions (upgrade the package that needs the newer peer, or pin the older one) and regenerate package-lock.json with `npm install`.
Use `--legacy-peer-deps` only as a temporary, documented workaround.

signatures.pattern: npm ci` can only install packages when your package\.json and package-lock\.json.*in sync|package-lock\.json.*(not in sync|out of date)|Missing: .* from lock file
signatures.title: package-lock.json out of sync with package.json
signatures.why: package.json changed without regenerating the lockfile, so `npm ci` refuses to install.
fix: Run `npm install` locally with the same Node version as the pipeline.
Commit the updated package-lock.json.

signatures.pattern: npm (ERR!|error) code E40[13]|npm (ERR!|error) 40[13] (Unauthorized|Forbidden)|Unable to authenticate, your authentication token seems to be invalid
signatures.title: npm feed authentication failed (401/403)
signatures.why: The pipeline could not authenticate to the private npm feed (e.g. Azure Artifacts): missing npmAuthenticate step, expired token, or the build identity lacks Reader on the feed.
fix: Add/verify the `npmAuthenticate@0` task (Azure Pipelines) or `setup-node` with registry-url + NODE_AUTH_TOKEN (GitHub Actions) before install.
Give the project build service identity at least Feed Reader on the feed (feed settings > Permissions).
Do not commit tokens in .npmrc.

signatures.pattern: The engine "node" is incompatible|Unsupported engine|error:0308010C:digital envelope routines
signatures.title: Node.js version on the agent does not match the project
signatures.why: The agent's Node version differs from what the project/engines field expects (0308010C = Node 17+ with an old webpack/OpenSSL).
fix: Pin Node in the pipeline: `NodeTool@0` versionSpec (Azure) or `actions/setup-node` node-version (GitHub) to the version in .nvmrc / engines.
Keep .nvmrc and the pipeline in sync.

signatures.pattern: JavaScript heap out of memory|Reached heap limit Allocation failed
signatures.title: Node build ran out of memory
signatures.why: The JS build/test exceeded Node's default heap on the agent.
fix: Set `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` for the build step.
Check for a recent dependency or bundle-size jump that caused it.

signatures.pattern: error NU1101: Unable to find package (?P<package>[\w.\-]+)
signatures.title: NuGet package {package} not found on configured feeds
signatures.why: The package/version is not on any feed the pipeline uses (private package not published, wrong nuget.config, or upstream source missing).
fix: Check the package name/version in the .csproj.
Make sure the pipeline restores with the repo's nuget.config (`feedsToUse: config`).
If it is an internal package, confirm it was published to the feed and the feed has the needed upstream sources.

signatures.pattern: error NU1301|Response status code does not indicate success: 401|NU1302|Unable to load the service index for source
signatures.title: NuGet feed unreachable or unauthorised
signatures.why: Restore could not read a feed's service index - usually 401 (auth) or an unreachable/private source.
fix: Add `NuGetAuthenticate@1` before restore (Azure) or configure credentials for the source (GitHub).
Give the build service identity Feed Reader on the Azure Artifacts feed.
If the source URL is wrong or retired, fix nuget.config.

signatures.pattern: (error|warning) NU1605.*Detected package downgrade: (?P<package>[\w.\-]+)
signatures.title: NuGet package downgrade detected ({package})
signatures.why: A project references a lower version of a package than a dependency requires; treated as an error.
fix: Reference the higher version of {package} directly in the affected project, or use central package management to align versions.

signatures.pattern: NETSDK1045|The current \.NET SDK does not support targeting|A compatible \.NET SDK was not found|global\.json
signatures.title: .NET SDK on the agent does not match the project
signatures.why: The project targets a newer .NET than the agent has, or global.json pins an SDK that is not installed.
fix: Add `UseDotNet@2` (Azure) or `actions/setup-dotnet` (GitHub) with the version from global.json / TargetFramework.

signatures.title: C# compile error {code} in {file}:{line}
signatures.why: The code does not compile on the agent: {msg}
fix: Open {file} at line {line}.
If it compiles locally, check for a file not committed, a case-sensitive path (Linux agents), or a missing package/project reference.

signatures.pattern: (?P<file>[\w\\/.\-]+\.tsx?)[(:](?P<line>\d+)[,:]\d+\)?:? - error (?P<code>TS\d+): (?P<msg>.+)|error (?P<code2>TS\d+): (?P<msg2>.+)
signatures.title: TypeScript compile error
signatures.why: tsc failed; the first error is usually the real one.
fix: Fix the first reported error; later errors often cascade from it.
Check the TypeScript version in the lockfile matches local.

signatures.pattern: error MSB(?P<code>\d{4}): (?P<msg>.+)
signatures.title: MSBuild error MSB{code}
signatures.why: {msg}
fix: Read the MSB error text; common causes are missing SDKs/workloads, wrong paths, or project reference problems.

signatures.pattern: Failed!\s+-\s+Failed:\s+(?P<failed>\d+)|Total tests:.*Failed:\s*[1-9]
signatures.title: {failed} .NET test(s) failed
signatures.why: Tests ran and some failed. Could be a real regression or a flaky test.
fix: See the failing test names below.
Run them locally; compare with the last green run to see if they are new failures (regression) or intermittent (flaky).

signatures.pattern: Tests:\s+(?P<failed>\d+) failed
signatures.title: {failed} Jest test(s) failed
signatures.why: Jest reported failing tests.
fix: See the failing tests (● lines).
Run `npx jest <file>` locally; check snapshot updates and time/timezone-dependent tests.

signatures.pattern: =+ .*?(?P<failed>\d+) failed
signatures.title: {failed} pytest test(s) failed
signatures.why: pytest reported failing tests.
fix: See the FAILED lines below.
Run `pytest -x <test id>` locally with the same Python version.

signatures.pattern: Tests run: \d+, Failures: (?P<failed>[1-9]\d*)|There are test failures
signatures.title: Maven/Gradle test failures
signatures.why: JUnit tests failed.
fix: Open the surefire report for the failing class.
Run `mvn -Dtest=<Class> test` locally.

signatures.pattern: coverage threshold for .* not met|Coverage for .* does not meet|ERROR: Coverage failure|coverage .* is below the (minimum|threshold)
signatures.title: Code coverage below the required threshold
signatures.why: Tests passed but coverage dropped under the gate.
fix: Add tests for the new/changed code (see the coverage report for uncovered files).
Do not lower the threshold without agreement.

signatures.pattern: ✖ \d+ problems? \((?P<errors>[1-9]\d*) errors?
signatures.title: Lint errors ({errors})
signatures.why: ESLint found errors; the pipeline treats them as failures.
fix: Run `npx eslint . --fix` locally, then fix what remains.
Make sure local ESLint config/version matches the pipeline.

signatures.pattern: QUALITY GATE STATUS: FAILED|Quality Gate (has )?failed
signatures.title: SonarQube/SonarCloud quality gate failed
signatures.why: New code breaks a quality gate condition (coverage, duplications, bugs, security hotspots).
fix: Open the Sonar dashboard link in the log to see which condition failed on new code.

signatures.pattern: AADSTS7000222|client secret keys for app .* are expired|AADSTS7000215
signatures.title: Service connection secret expired or invalid (Entra ID)
signatures.why: The Azure service connection uses an app registration secret that expired or is wrong. Every pipeline using that connection fails at login.
fix: A pipeline admin should convert the service connection to **workload identity federation** (no secret to expire) - Project settings > Service connections > Convert.
Short-term: rotate the secret on the app registration and update the connection.
Add an expiry alert for remaining secret-based connections.

signatures.pattern: AADSTS700213|AADSTS70021|No matching federated identity record found
signatures.title: Workload identity federation: no matching federated credential
signatures.why: The federated credential on the app registration/managed identity does not match the pipeline's issuer/subject (e.g. renamed service connection or project).
fix: Compare the subject shown in the error with the federated credential (`sc://<org>/<project>/<service connection>` for Azure DevOps; `repo:<org>/<repo>:environment:<env>` etc. for GitHub).
An admin updates the federated credential to the exact subject.

signatures.pattern: AADSTS700016
signatures.title: App registration not found in the tenant
signatures.why: The service connection points at an app registration that was deleted or is in another tenant.
fix: An admin recreates/re-points the service connection to a valid identity.

signatures.pattern: does not have secrets? (get|list) permission on key vault|ForbiddenByRbac|ForbiddenByPolicy|ForbiddenByFirewall|Caller was not found on any access policy|Client address is not authorized and caller is not a trusted service
signatures.title: Key Vault refused the pipeline identity
signatures.why: The AzureKeyVault task (or az keyvault) was denied: the service connection identity has no Get/List on secrets (RBAC role or access policy), or the vault firewall blocks the agent (ForbiddenByFirewall).
fix: Permissions: give the service connection identity the `Key Vault Secrets User` role on the vault (RBAC vaults) or an access policy with Get and List on secrets (access-policy vaults).
Firewall: run the job on agents inside the vault's network (self-hosted or managed pool with a private endpoint) instead of opening the vault to hosted-agent IP ranges.
Narrow the task's SecretsFilter to the secrets this pipeline needs.

signatures.pattern: AuthorizationFailed|does not have authorization to perform action '(?P<action>[^']+)'
signatures.title: Pipeline identity lacks permission ({action})
signatures.why: The service connection's identity is missing an RBAC role for this action on the target scope.
fix: Grant the least-privilege built-in role that includes '{action}' on the narrowest scope (resource group), via your platform team's access process.
Do not grant Owner/Contributor at subscription scope to fix one action.

signatures.pattern: service connection (?P<name>.+?) which could not be found|The service connection does not exist|has not been authorized for use|could not find a service connection
signatures.title: Service connection not found or not authorised for this pipeline
signatures.why: The YAML references a service connection that doesn't exist, was renamed, or this pipeline hasn't been granted access to.
fix: Check the connection name in YAML matches Project settings > Service connections exactly.
An admin grants this pipeline permission to use it (Security > Pipeline permissions).

signatures.title: Pipeline variable $({var}) is not defined
signatures.why: Azure Pipelines leaves `$(name)` literally in the command when the variable doesn't exist (missing variable group link, typo, or secret not mapped).
fix: Check the variable name spelling and that the variable group is linked (`variables: - group: ...`).
Secret variables are not auto-mapped into scripts - pass them via `env:`.

signatures.pattern: toomanyrequests: You have reached your pull rate limit
signatures.title: Docker Hub pull rate limit
signatures.why: Anonymous/free Docker Hub pulls are rate limited; shared agents hit it often.
fix: Pull base images from your ACR/ECR mirror, or authenticate to Docker Hub (docker login with a service account) before pulling.

signatures.pattern: manifest unknown|manifest for (?P<image>\S+) not found|pull access denied for (?P<image2>\S+)
signatures.title: Container image or tag not found / not accessible
signatures.why: The image tag doesn't exist (typo, not pushed yet, deleted) or the registry needs login.
fix: Verify the tag exists in the registry.
Add a login step for private registries; check the push job ran before this one.

signatures.pattern: No space left on device|There is not enough space on the disk|ENOSPC
signatures.title: Agent ran out of disk space
signatures.why: Build outputs, Docker layers or caches filled the agent disk.
fix: Clean up in the job (`docker system prune -af`, remove large caches) or use a larger agent.
For self-hosted agents, the platform team should add disk cleanup.

signatures.pattern: Unable to locate executable file: '(?P<tool>[^']+)'|(?P<tool2>[\w.\-]+): command not found|'(?P<tool3>[\w.\-]+)' is not recognized as an internal or external command
signatures.title: Tool not found on the agent
signatures.why: The step needs a tool the agent image doesn't have - often after a hosted image update (e.g. ubuntu/windows-latest moved to a new version).
fix: Install the tool explicitly in the pipeline (UsePythonVersion, NodeTool, setup-* actions) instead of relying on the image.
Pin the agent image (e.g. ubuntu-24.04) rather than *-latest if needed.

signatures.pattern: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named '(?P<module>[\w.]+)'
signatures.title: Python module '{module}' not installed
signatures.why: The dependency isn't in requirements / wasn't installed in the environment the step uses.
fix: Add {module} to requirements.txt / pyproject and make sure the install step runs in the same Python environment.

signatures.pattern: ResolutionImpossible|Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement (?P<req>\S+)
signatures.title: pip could not resolve dependencies
signatures.why: Conflicting or unavailable package versions for this Python version/platform.
fix: Check the Python version on the agent vs local.
Relax or align the conflicting pins.

signatures.pattern: Could not transfer artifact (?P<artifact>\S+) from/to (?P<repo>\S+) .*(status code: 40[13]|Unauthorized|Forbidden|not authorized)|Return code is: 40[13]
signatures.title: Maven repository refused the credentials (401/403)
signatures.why: Maven reached the repository but was refused: no <server> credentials whose id matches the repository id, an expired token, or the build identity has no read access to the feed.
fix: Make the <server><id> in settings.xml match the <repository><id> in the POM exactly (case-sensitive).
Azure Pipelines: add `MavenAuthenticate@0` for the feed before the build. GitHub Actions: `actions/setup-java` with server-id, server-username and server-password pointing at secrets.
Give the build identity Reader on the feed; never commit credentials in settings.xml.

signatures.pattern: Could not resolve dependencies for project|Failed to collect dependencies|Could not resolve all files for configuration
signatures.title: Maven/Gradle dependency resolution failed
signatures.why: Artifact missing from repositories or repository auth failed.
fix: Check the artifact coordinates and the repository/feed credentials (MavenAuthenticate@0 for Azure Artifacts).

signatures.pattern: Error acquiring the state lock
signatures.title: Terraform state is locked
signatures.why: Another run holds the state lock, or a previous run crashed and left a stale lock.
fix: Check whether another pipeline run is in progress; wait for it.
Only if the lock is confirmed stale, a human runs `terraform force-unlock <LOCK_ID>` (never automated).

signatures.pattern: QuotaExceeded|SkuNotAvailable|exceeding approved (?P<family>[\w ]+?) quota|OperationNotAllowed.*quota
signatures.title: Azure capacity: quota exceeded or size not available in the region
signatures.why: The subscription hit a vCPU/resource quota, or the requested SKU is not offered (or is restricted) in that region or zone. The template itself is fine.
fix: Check usage and limits read-only: `az vm list-usage --location <region> -o table` and `az vm list-skus --location <region> --size <sku> -o table` (see Restrictions).
Ask the subscription owner for a quota increase, or choose another size, zone or region in the parameters.
Remove leftover test resources that use up the quota.

signatures.pattern: InvalidTemplate(Deployment)?|DeploymentFailed|"code":\s*"(?P<code>[A-Za-z]+)".*"message"
signatures.title: Azure deployment (ARM/Bicep) failed
signatures.why: The template or its parameters were rejected, or a resource failed to deploy - the inner error code says why.
fix: Find the innermost `code`/`message` in the log.
Reproduce with `az deployment group what-if` (read-only) against the same parameters.

signatures.pattern: fatal: could not read Username|Authentication failed for|Permission denied \(publickey\)|TF401019|remote: Repository not found
signatures.title: Git authentication failed (checkout of a repo/submodule)
signatures.why: The job's identity can't read a repository it needs (other repo, submodule, or private package from git).
fix: Azure: grant the project build service Read on the other repo and use `checkout: git://Project/Repo` or persistCredentials.
GitHub: use a token/app with access to that repo for checkout.

signatures.pattern: java\.lang\.OutOfMemoryError: (?P<kind>Java heap space|Metaspace|GC overhead limit exceeded)|Gradle build daemon disappeared unexpectedly|Expiring Daemon because JVM heap space is exhausted
signatures.title: JVM ran out of memory (Gradle/Maven build)
signatures.why: The Gradle daemon, Kotlin compiler or Maven JVM exceeded its heap or metaspace. The defaults are small for large multi-module builds and hosted agents have limited RAM.
fix: Set JVM memory in gradle.properties: `org.gradle.jvmargs=-Xmx4g -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=1g` (Maven: `MAVEN_OPTS=-Xmx4g`).
Limit parallel workers on small agents (`org.gradle.workers.max=2`) or use a larger agent.
Check whether a recent change (new module, code generation, test fork settings) caused the jump.

signatures.pattern: verifying (?P<module>\S+): checksum mismatch|does NOT match (an earlier download recorded in go\.sum|the one reported by the checksum)
signatures.title: Go module checksum mismatch
signatures.why: The downloaded module content differs from go.sum: the version was re-tagged upstream, a proxy served different content, or go.sum was edited by hand. Treat it as a possible supply-chain problem until explained.
fix: Do not delete go.sum lines to make it pass. Compare locally with `go mod download -json <module>@<version>` against the public checksum database.
For private modules, set GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB for their path and make every build use the same GOPROXY.
If upstream re-tagged a release, move to a new version instead of accepting changed content for the same version.

signatures.pattern: error\[E(?P<code>\d{4})\]: (?P<msg>.+)
signatures.title: Rust compile error E{code}
signatures.why: The crate does not compile on the agent: {msg}
fix: Open the file and line from the ` --> src/...:line:col` line under the error.
Build locally with the pipeline's toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml) and `cargo build --locked`; `rustc --explain E{code}` describes the error.

signatures.pattern: the lock file (?P<lock>\S+) needs to be updated but --locked was passed|cannot update the lock file (?P<lock2>\S+) because --locked was passed
signatures.title: Cargo.lock is out of date (--locked)
signatures.why: Cargo.toml changed without regenerating Cargo.lock, and the pipeline builds with --locked, so cargo refuses to change the lockfile.
fix: Run `cargo build` (or `cargo update -w`) locally and commit Cargo.lock.
Keep --locked in CI; it is what caught this.

signatures.pattern: error: externally-managed-environment|This environment is externally managed
signatures.title: pip refused to install into the system Python (PEP 668)
signatures.why: Newer images (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12, Homebrew Python) mark the system Python as externally managed, so `pip install` outside a virtual environment is blocked.
fix: Install a pipeline Python first (`UsePythonVersion@0` / `actions/setup-python`) or create a venv (`python -m venv .venv`, then use .venv/bin/pip).
Use pipx for command-line tools.
`--break-system-packages` is only acceptable inside throwaway containers.

signatures.pattern: npm (ERR!|error) (code E404|404 Not Found)|'(?P<package>[^'\s]+)' is not in (this|the npm) registry
signatures.title: npm package or version not found in the registry (E404)
signatures.why: A package in package.json or the lockfile does not exist on the registry the agent uses: a typo, a private or scoped package looked up on the public registry (missing scope mapping), or an unpublished version.
fix: Read the `404 Not Found - GET <url>` line to see which package and which registry.
For a private or scoped package, map the scope in .npmrc (`@scope:registry=<feed url>`) and authenticate (npmAuthenticate@0 / setup-node registry-url).
If the version was unpublished, move to an existing version and regenerate the lockfile.

signatures.pattern: Not authorized\. (Please check the (user token|properties)|Analyzing this project requires authentication)|You're not authorized to (run analysis|analyze this project)
signatures.title: SonarQube/SonarCloud rejected the analysis token
signatures.why: The scanner token is missing, expired or revoked, lacks Execute Analysis on the project, or the project key does not exist and the token may not create it.
fix: Regenerate the token and update the Sonar service connection or the SONAR_TOKEN secret (pipeline admin).
Check that the project key in the pipeline matches the Sonar project and the token's user has Execute Analysis.
Newer SonarQube versions read the token from sonar.token (sonar.login is deprecated).

signatures.pattern: reached the maximum number of requests that can run for parallelism type|No hosted parallelism has been purchased or granted
signatures.title: No free parallel job for this pipeline
signatures.why: The organisation's parallel-job limit is in use (runs wait until one frees), or no hosted parallelism is granted at all (new organisations must request the free grant).
fix: Check Organization settings > Parallel jobs for in-use versus purchased.
Buy more Microsoft-hosted parallel jobs, request the free grant, or add self-hosted agents.
Cut waste: batch CI triggers (`batch: true`), cancel superseded PR runs (`autoCancel`), and shorten long-held jobs.

signatures.pattern: No agent found in pool (?P<pool>.+?) which satisfies the (specified|following) demands?
signatures.title: No agent in pool {pool} satisfies the job's demands
signatures.why: The job asks for a capability (demands, a tool, an OS) that no online agent in that pool has, or every matching agent is offline or disabled.
fix: Compare the job's `demands:` with the agents' capabilities (Organization settings > Agent pools > {pool} > Agents).
Drop demands that are not needed or install the tool in the job instead.
If the matching agents are offline, the platform team brings them back or adds capacity.

signatures.pattern: Resource not accessible by integration|Resource not accessible by personal access token
signatures.title: GITHUB_TOKEN lacks the permission for this API call
signatures.why: The workflow token has fewer scopes than the step needs (for example commenting on a PR, pushing a tag, writing packages). Pull requests from forks always get a read-only token.
fix: Grant only the needed scope on this job, e.g. `permissions: pull-requests: write` or `contents: write`.
For fork PRs, move the write action into a separate workflow triggered by workflow_run instead of widening the token.
A read-only default for the organisation is correct; declare permissions per job.

signatures.pattern: recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased
signatures.title: GitHub Actions blocked by billing or spending limit
signatures.why: The account ran out of included minutes and the spending limit (or a failed payment) stops new jobs from starting.
fix: An organisation owner checks Settings > Billing (usage, spending limit, payment method).
Reduce minutes: cancel superseded runs with `concurrency:`, cache dependencies, and skip workflows for docs-only changes (`paths-ignore`).

signatures.pattern: Input required and not supplied: (?P<input>[\w-]+)
signatures.title: Action input '{input}' is required but empty
signatures.why: The action got an empty value for a required input, usually a secret that does not exist in this repo or environment, or is not passed to workflows from forks or Dependabot.
fix: Check the secret or variable used for {input} in the `with:` block and that it exists at repository, environment or organisation level.
Fork and Dependabot pull requests do not receive repository secrets: skip the step for them or use Dependabot secrets.

signatures.pattern: another operation \(install/upgrade/rollback\) is in progress
signatures.title: Helm release locked by an earlier unfinished operation
signatures.why: A previous helm install/upgrade was interrupted (cancelled job, timeout) and left the release in a pending state, so Helm refuses a new operation.
fix: Inspect read-only: `helm history <release> -n <namespace>` shows the pending revision.
A person with cluster access rolls back to the last deployed revision (`helm rollback <release> <revision>`) after confirming no other deploy is running; do not automate this.
Prevent it: `helm upgrade --install --atomic --wait --timeout 10m` and one deploy at a time per environment (exclusive lock check / GitHub `concurrency:`).

signatures.pattern: You must be logged in to the server \(Unauthorized\)|the server has asked for the client to provide credentials
signatures.title: Kubernetes API rejected the pipeline credentials (Unauthorized)
signatures.why: The kubeconfig token or certificate is expired or invalid: an old kubeconfig stored as a secret, a rotated cluster certificate, or an AKS cluster with Entra ID auth where kubelogin did not convert the kubeconfig.
fix: Get credentials inside the job from the service connection (Kubernetes tasks with an Azure Resource Manager connection, or `az aks get-credentials` followed by `kubelogin convert-kubeconfig -l azurecli`).
Do not store long-lived kubeconfigs as secrets; prefer workload identity federation.
If the cluster certificate was rotated, the pipeline admin updates the Kubernetes service connection.

signatures.pattern: Executable doesn't exist at \S*ms-playwright|Looks like Playwright (Test or Playwright )?was just installed or updated
signatures.title: Playwright browsers are not installed on the agent
signatures.why: The Playwright package is installed but its browsers are not (they live outside node_modules), or the cached browsers are for a different Playwright version.
fix: Run `npx playwright install --with-deps` (same version as @playwright/test in the lockfile) before the tests.
Cache the browser folder (~/.cache/ms-playwright on Linux) keyed on the Playwright version, or run in the Playwright container image of that version.

signatures.pattern: The cypress npm package is installed, but the Cypress binary is missing|No version of Cypress is installed in
signatures.title: Cypress binary missing on the agent
signatures.why: node_modules came from a cache (or CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY=0 was set) but the Cypress binary lives in a separate cache folder that was not restored.
fix: Cache the binary folder too (~/.cache/Cypress, or set CYPRESS_CACHE_FOLDER inside the workspace) keyed on the lockfile, or run `npx cypress install` after restoring node_modules.
On GitHub, cypress-io/github-action restores both caches.

signatures.pattern: certificate has expired|CERT_HAS_EXPIRED|unable to get local issuer certificate|SSL certificate problem|self[- ]signed certificate in certificate chain
signatures.title: TLS certificate problem
signatures.why: An expired certificate on a feed/endpoint, or a corporate proxy's certificate not trusted on the agent.
fix: Check which host failed; if it's a corporate proxy, the platform team adds the root CA to the agent image - do not disable TLS verification.

signatures.pattern: ETIMEDOUT|ECONNRESET|Connection timed out|Could not resolve host|getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND|503 Service Unavailable|EAI_AGAIN
signatures.title: Network error reaching an external service
signatures.why: Transient network failure, an outage of the remote service, or the agent can't reach a private endpoint.
fix: Re-run once; if it passes, add retries for that step.
If it keeps failing on self-hosted agents, check firewall/private DNS for that host.

signatures.pattern: ran longer than the maximum time|has exceeded the maximum execution time|timed out after \d+|The job was canceled because it exceeded
signatures.title: Job timed out
signatures.why: The job hit its time limit - a hang (waiting for input, deadlock, network) or a genuinely slower build.
fix: Find the last step that was running and what it was waiting for.
Raise `timeoutInMinutes` only if the build is legitimately slower.

signatures.pattern: The operation was canceled|##\[error\]The job was canceled|Canceling since a higher priority waiting request
signatures.title: Job was cancelled
signatures.why: Cancelled by a user, a newer run, or a timeout - look for an earlier error.
fix: Check whether a newer commit superseded this run before investigating further.
